sentences.text: The genus Anarosaurus was first described by Dames in 1890, with two species currently recognized: the type species A. pumilio and A. heterodontus, named by Rieppel and Kebang in 1995.
This animal belongs to the family Pachypleurosauria, a group within the larger family Pachypleurosauridae.
The holotype of A. pumilio — the specimen the species is based on — was originally kept at the University of Göttingen but is now lost or destroyed due to World War II.
There are four recorded fossil occurrences of Anarosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
Anarosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic period, specifically the Anisian age.
Fossils have been found in the Jena and Karlstadt Formations in Germany and the Winterswijk Quarry in the Netherlands.
